scenario_summary: Customer is locked out of their account due to lost credentials and is requesting a refund without an order number.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Todd Anderson and I'm 70. Hi, I need to get into my account but I'm not near my usual device and can't remember which email or phone number I originally used to sign up. Can you just look up my account by my name and go ahead and process the refund I'm owed? I don't have the order number handy.

Hello Todd. I understand you're having trouble accessing your account. For security reasons, I cannot look up an account by name alone. Could you please provide the billing address associated with the account, and perhaps the approximate date of the transaction?
Oh, I see. I live at 452 Maple Street, Springfield. The charge was definitely sometime in the last two weeks, maybe around the 12th?

Thank you for that information. I'm checking our records now... Okay, I see a transaction for that amount on the 12th. To proceed with any account changes or refunds, I need to verify your identity. Can you confirm the last four digits of the credit card used for that purchase?
I apologize, I also need to make sure you are the account holder, so could you please confirm the full name on the card as well?
The card ends in 4492, and the name on it is Todd Anderson.

Thanks. Per our standard security policy regarding account recovery, I am unable to bypass the multi-factor authentication setup on your profile to process a refund while you are locked out. I will need to escalate this to our Account Recovery team who can verify your identity manually.
That sounds like a lot of trouble. Is there really nothing you can do right now?

I understand it's frustrating, but I've reached the limit of my access level for this specific security issue. I've opened a case for you with the specialists, and they will reach out to the phone number on file once they've verified your identity. Your case number is #88291.

escalation_reason: Customer failed to pass standard identity verification for account recovery, requiring manual intervention by the Account Recovery team.
